name_reason: Conforms to fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>; descriptor accurately names the behavior (mark a runtime char as having acted this turn by setting flags bit 0x80). No Ghidra address residue.
purpose: Set the acted-this-turn flag (bit 0x80 / CHARFLAG_ACTED) on the indexed runtime char so the rest of the turn machinery treats it as having taken its action.
logic_summary: Computes the base address of runtime_char[char_idx] (data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr + char_idx*RUNTIME_CHAR_SIZE), then ORs CHARFLAG_ACTED (0x80) into the flags byte at offset 5. Single basic block, no branches. (Ghidra also shows a leading __CHK(4) Watcom stack-probe call.)

params.name: char_idx
params.semantics: Index into the runtime_char array of the char to mark as acted. Callers pass a loop index over chars (e.g. fd2_apply_end_turn_regen passes (uint32)i).
params.reason: Descriptive and accurate (array index of the char); no address residue.

comment_original_issue: Original src comment was correct but terse (only stated 'set flags bit 0x80'); did not note who consumes the bit.
notes: src writes via byte pointer pChar[5] |= CHARFLAG_ACTED; Ghidra writes via struct field .bFlags |= 0x80. Both agree on offset 5 and bit 0x80, so they are consistent (equivalence already verified upstream). The fd2-knowledge struct doc labels offset 0x0D as the action-status byte from a different memory-hack table/version; that is a struct-doc note, not a discrepancy in this symbol, so no issue raised. reads_globals/writes_globals both list data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr because the |= is a read-modify-write of that array's flags byte (pointer global itself is only read).
